title: Pruned-dense baseline: DINOv2-small at r56, channel-magnitude pruning to {50%, 25%}, ridge readout
question: Where does the train-big-then-prune side of the comparison sit at the sealed dense data level? M144 is a MEASURING STICK (no win/loss gate).

registration_notes.N105.1: The cached torch DINOv2-small weights (M109 path), the M107 feature definition (CLS + mean patch tokens, 768 cols), resolution 56 (the sealed r56 arm), 138k train rows (the sealed dense ladder level).
registration_notes.N105.2: Structured channel pruning by magnitude on the attention + MLP matrices only: attention heads scored by the L2 norm of their concatenated q/k/v output rows; MLP units by fc1 row L2. A dropped unit's output rows AND the next matrix's matching input columns AND the biases are zeroed, so the pruned forward pass equals the kept subnetwork exactly. keep in {1.0, 0.5, 0.25}; achieved nonzero-parameter fractions are reported, never assumed.
registration_notes.N105.3: Anchors: t1 the in-run ONNX-vs-torch parity guard at r56 (bound 1e-4, the sealed M109 guard); t2 the unpruned torch re-encode must reproduce the sealed r56 read 0.245014492753623 within 0.002.
registration_notes.N105.4: Effective MACs: the sealed analytic ledger scaled by the kept channel fractions (projections x head_keep, attention x head_keep^2, mlp x mlp_keep). The GPU computes the zeroed units; only the reported MACs are pruned — same convention as the sealed ledger exclusions, disclosed.
registration_notes.N105.5: Smoke runs declare _smoke_note and MUST refuse the sealed output directory.

arms.note: keep=1.0 is the unpruned torch re-encode (the t2 anchor arm).

frontier_context.note: sparse 138k values from the sealed C2/C3/C4/C3b evidence; full-data best = the promoted SPM+sqrt recipe.
